title: Unreasonable Hospitality
alternate_titles: Unreasonable Hospitality: The Remarkable Power of Giving People More Than They Expect

contents: The Eleven Madison Park story: from struggling two-star brasserie to the World's 50 Best number one
The distinction between service and hospitality
Being unreasonable: the 95/5 rule and spending the last five percent foolishly
Dreamweavers: staffing for bespoke gestures, from the street-cart hot dog to the sledding trip
Leading the team: praise and criticism with intention, charitable assumptions, being the swan
One size fits one: making every guest feel seen
Hospitality as a strategy any business can choose

audiences: People running or managing service businesses of any kind
Leaders building team culture around customer care
Fans of The Bear curious about the book behind season two

sources.title: Unreasonable Hospitality
sources.supports: Title, subtitle, imprint, publication date, ISBN, 288 pages, formats, the publisher's description of the transformation story and signature gestures (sledding trip, beach dining room), and the claim that every business can choose to be a hospitality business.
sources.limitations: Authoritative for publication facts; promotional in tone.

sources.title: Unreasonable Hospitality is good business: 5 lessons from Will Guidara
sources.supports: The book's named concepts as applied by business readers: the 95/5 rule, dreamweavers, the one-inch rule, charitable assumptions, being the swan, and the simplified mission statement.
sources.limitations: Enthusiast application piece rather than critical review.
